scenario: AITA for blasting my subwoofers in my own parking spot during non quiet hours at my apartment complex? | Posting from a throwaway for whatever reason, just don't want this to blend into my other subs. So basically my car is my life. I have a tuned Subaru Impreza WRX STI that is my hobby, my transportation, my life, I'm more comfortable behind the wheel than I am in my own bed. Its not quite as fast as I want it but it looks amazing and the sound system is seriously as good as it can be. I live in a large apartment complex in Tucson, I'm guessing probably 100 units or so. Not sure. Anyways the complex is really cool because a lot of places won't let you work on your car, well I can pay an extra premium every month to get a mechanics spot under shade. It's an extra 2 bills a month but so worth it. When I work on my car I BLAST my system. It helps me think and focus. Also important to note our complex has quiet hours between and 10pm and 8am, I follow these to the letter but I do need to work on my car so some Saturday's and Sunday's I crank shit from 8:01am to 9:59pm. I am not breaking any rules at all. I moved in in January and this Sunday was apparently a major problem. I had two people ask me to turn it down. I totally did but one came back and said its not the volume, it's the bass, can I turn the bass down. I said I would try but I guess that wasn't good enough because he came down a third time. Finally I told him I paid for the spot, I wasn't breaking any rules, I'd only be out there until 10pm. He said his kids had to go to bed at 8:30 and the bass from my car was rattling his walls. I told him I'd done my best to accommodate him but I was done. He told me he'd call the police (who never showed) and talk to management. I just stopped responding to him and cranked my system to drown our his barking. I worked on my car until 9:59 when I turned my system off. I got an email from my apartment manager asking if she could come by. She's really cool and I want to help her but I feel like I'm paying extra for the mechanics spot, I'm not breaking any rules and that guy had no right to talk to me like that. She said she managed a nice place and she's gotten complaint after complaint about my car. I told her I was sorry but I was still well within my rights and not breaking rules. She asked me to please consider for her sake using headphones Or earbuds if music is that important to me. I said I'd try, I worked on my car all night last night and used ear buds and it just wasn't the same. I spent thousands of dollars and so much time to tune my system perfectly and to not use it when I want sucks. I want to help her out but am I even being an asshole in the first place?

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: **1 (Yes, you're the asshole)** Here's why, broken down objectively: ### ️ **You're not "breaking rules" in a technical sense... but you * are* violating community standards.** - **"Quiet hours" (10pm–8am) are only part of the equation.** Most lease agreements explicitly prohibit * " unreasonably disturbing noise"* ** at any time**— even outside designated quiet hours. Bass that rattles walls, vibrates structures, or disrupts sleep (e.g., a family with kids needing to sleep at 8:30pm) is * always* considered " unreasonably disturbing," regardless of the time of day. - **" Mechanics spot" ≠ " private concert venue."** The extra fee you pay is for * space to work on your car*, not a license to blast bass. The purpose of the spot is for repairs, not recreational audio playback. If you were * actually* working on the car (e.g., changing oil, fixing brakes), noise would be more defensible—but you're using it as a personal sound system. ### ️ **B bass is a known disruptor, and " it's not about volume" is the key issue.** - Low-frequency bass travels through walls, floors, and air more easily than higher frequencies. It can cause physical vibrations that disturb sleep, concentration, and even cause structural stress in apartments. This isn't " sensitivity"— it's physics. - **Multiple complaints from management confirm this isn't just one person being " difficult."** If * several* neighbors are reporting the same issue (especially with specific details like " rattling walls"), it's a clear pattern of disruption. Management wouldn't reach out if this were a trivial matter. ### ️ **" I paid extra" doesn't override your lease obligations.** - Leases are binding contracts. **" I paid for the spot" is irrelevant** because: - The spot is for * car maintenance*, not music playback. - All residents ( even those paying extra for special amenities) must comply with noise policies. - **" I'm within my rights" is a myth here.** Your " rights" end where your neighbor's right to peaceful enjoyment begins. ### ️ **You're being unreasonable in your response.** - **" I'll try earbuds... but it's not the same" is a non-st solution.** If you * truly* value your car's sound system, you could: - Use it * only* when no one is home (e.g., during work hours). - Install soundproofing in your car (e.g., bass blockers, dampening materials). - Use a portable Bluetooth speaker outside the complex (e.g., in a park). - **" I cranked it to drown out his barking" is escalatory and immature.** This is not " standing your ground"— it's intentionally making the situation worse. ### 💡 **The real issue:** You're prioritizing your personal enjoyment over the basic right of others to live without structural vibrations from bass. **This isn't about " being an audiophile"— it's about respecting shared living spaces.** If you * must* enjoy your car's sound system, do it in a way that doesn't physically disturb others (e.g., at a drive-in theater, on a closed road, or in a designated car audio event). **Final verdict:** **1 (Yes, you're the asshole)** because you're causing a documented disturbance that violates the spirit of your lease, even if not the letter. Management is right to ask you to compromise— and your refusal to do so ( beyond a half-hearted " I'll try earbuds") is inconsiderate. **Fix this:** - Use earbuds * consistently* while working on the car. - Apologize to neighbors and management. - If you can't compromise, consider moving to a property with a garage or more space (e.g., a house with a driveway). - **Remember:** " I paid extra" never justifies making others' lives worse. That's not " passion"— it's entitled behavior.
